batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 distinct IDs together with their supplied premeasurement QGeoGNN predictions. Prioritize unmeasured condition tuples that form interpretable solvent-response contrasts, a controlled loading contrast, and ordinary-regime calibration points. Increasing PE/EA means decreasing EA fraction and weaker normal-phase eluent; 0/1 is pure EA. Use structural comparisons and measured endpoint behavior without imposing universal monotonic solvent or loading responses.

choices.reason: Measure m73 at 0/1 and 50 ul near the anomalous pure-EA observation 2732471e4009311396ed, whose measured V1 exceeds V2. The current prediction is 11.35/17.68 mL. This neighboring loading point tests whether the unusual onset is localized or persists across the recorded pure-EA condition.

Pair m73 at 1/1 with its selected 0/1 point, holding density, sample volume, loading solvent, and loading-solvent volume fixed. Predicted onset falls from about 11.35 to 4.35 mL as eluent becomes weaker. Both labels are needed to assess this reversal without interpreting the invalid endpoint ordering in 2732471e4009311396ed as established chemistry.

m98 at 2/1 and 100 ul tests the predicted rise to 7.97/17.11 mL from the measured 1/1 point 038c2ece456c59cf6285 at 4.55/9.32 mL. This fills a missing response region for a fused aromatic acetate ester and distinguishes a substantial early condition response from extrapolation of the late regime.

The matched m98 10/1 point extends the selected 2/1 condition at identical loading, with prediction 12.96/26.90 mL. Together with the measured 50/1, 150-ul anchor 67fa39740fcf946a3154, it tests whether onset progressively delays or finish broadens disproportionately as EA fraction decreases.

m185 at 1/1 and 50 ul probes the predicted 8.13/19.29 mL response beyond its measured pure-EA anchor abcfcb23dbe2574a2389 at 3.94/7.96 mL. The much earlier dibromo analogue in 5f18493c09da8b07b64a makes the predicted fluorinated-versus-brominated difference worth testing; the structural explanation remains a hypothesis.

m185 at 5/1 and 50 ul forms a solvent-response pair with its selected 1/1 point. Its predicted 10.98/26.38 mL interval is substantially later than the ordinary dibromobenzaldehyde behavior in c098b72af1f4e81425e7. The labels can teach substituent-environment effects beyond simply recognizing an aromatic aldehyde.

The m185 5/1, 150-ul point triples loading relative to the selected 50-ul point while keeping the other recorded conditions fixed. Predictions are nearly identical despite the amount change from 65.85 to 197.55 mg. This controlled contrast tests loading sensitivity without assuming that the irregular m177 behavior generalizes.

m199 at 5/1 and 150 ul establishes a sulfoxide response point before the selected 10/1 condition. The measured 2/1, lower-loading reference 9ddc2e8babb52ee8e772 is 14.26/26.03 mL, while this prediction is 13.83/26.04 mL. The new same-loading solvent pair will distinguish a plateau from a later upturn.

m199 at 10/1 and 150 ul is predicted at 23.15/39.45 mL versus 13.83/26.04 mL at the selected 5/1 point. The pair tests whether weaker eluent delays both endpoints for this strong acceptor, supplying supervision for a sulfur-oxygen environment that should not inherit carbonyl-family response curves automatically.

m92 at 5/1 and 50 ul fills the alpha-ketoester curve below the measured 10/1 point 0389a6366b3a51fad8b5. Its 9.10/23.00 mL prediction provides an intermediate anchor for interpreting the unusual predicted 20/1 onset and the much broader measured 50/1 finish in 7caf1db075b91197ba34.

m92 at 20/1 and 50 ul holds loading and EA loading-solvent conditions fixed relative to the selected 5/1 and measured 10/1 points. Predicted onset drops to 5.74 mL. The higher-loading 20/1 observation e9dc948c0e68a88eb621 is also early, but this label is needed to separate solvent response from that loading difference.

m75 at 10/1 and 100 ul supplies the loading-matched reference for its selected 20/1 point. The measured 10/1, 50-ul records fa1a4a2aa332b091b615 and ce3b9d9cbe1699c7eef9 are later than the measured 50/1 point 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e. This additional loading level tests how broadly that recorded reversal applies.

m75 at 20/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 8.68/15.14 mL, earlier than its selected 10/1 prediction of 11.27/19.08 mL. Measuring the matched pair can locate a turnover in this phenylmalonate response and prevent an inappropriate universal late correction across diesters.

m87 is ethyl 4-methoxybenzoate. Its 2/1, 100-ul point tests a broad predicted finish of 23.12 mL near the measured higher-loading 2/1 reference 0637945ca309d8122e64. This anchors the selected 5/1 comparison after the recent 20/1 overprediction in eed75e5b0d9c27fa754c.

The matched m87 5/1 point is predicted to finish slightly earlier than 2/1 despite weaker eluent. Measuring both at 100 ul tests whether this is a real plateau or reversal, and whether the model has transferred excessive retention from amino esters to a donor-free methoxy ester.

m85 at 5/1 and 150 ul begins a matched ethyl 4-fluorobenzoate contrast. Its prediction is 9.38/17.92 mL, with both endpoints later than the selected 10/1 prediction. This tests an unmeasured response region in a simple ester family with several halogenated analogues.

m85 at 10/1 and 150 ul completes the matched pair, predicted at 6.19/14.33 mL. The recorded 20/1 reference 0dd38abec3981f296cfb is later again, although at lower loading. The pair will establish whether the model's intermediate-ratio dip deserves supervision as a local relationship.

m45 at 20/1 and 150 ul extends a loading series: b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1 at 50 ul and e6605c23fb1943a6b848 at 100 ul have substantially different onsets. This label tests continuation versus irregular variation at higher loading. The reversed, near-zero 50/1 record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 is treated as anomalous evidence.

m104 at 20/1 and 100 ul tests the predicted return to an ordinary 4.41/10.27 mL interval. The measured 50/1 point 302e458c5ed2285ca328 remains ordinary, unlike several other amino esters. This missing condition helps learn the specific ortho-amino methyl ester response rather than a generic amine-driven late regime.

m18 at 1/1 and 100 ul has a slightly reversed predicted interval, 4.367/4.354 mL. Nearby measured conditions 192516b3cc0500ef715b and 68c511d842fc030aa84b have positive, several-mL intervals. This common-condition label tests excessive finish compression for a hydrophobic long-chain acrylate.

m71 at 1/1 and 100 ul is predicted to finish at 4.36 mL, whereas pure-EA and 2/1 references e4a7e43d15fcdee2ba1d and 0f8ae9a2f5ed927d4a08 finish near 9 mL. This probes a potentially overcompressed ordinary interval in a very lipophilic thiophene environment, independently of selecting broad late predictions.

m97 at 50/1 and 100 ul tests extrapolation beyond the measured 20/1 point 80762b40f399bb68342a. Its predicted 19.76/43.03 mL interval can be compared with the selected constitutional-isomer m101 point, teaching whether ester connectivity changes the weak-eluent response beyond the already similar intermediate-ratio behavior.

m101 at 50/1 and approximately 150 mg is predicted at 18.48/42.30 mL, close to the selected m97 prediction at 144.5 mg. With da2750836408eb0e09a7 providing its measured 20/1 reference, this is a useful near-mass-matched structural-isomer comparison of benzoate versus phenylacetate connectivity.

m51 at 10/1 and 50 ul completes a lower-loading extension around bad24d96575f423fe4fd at 100 ul. The prediction is 33.96/57.21 mL. Together with the measured 5/1 low-loading point bf09d868ed4d68a97b40, this tests onset and finish responses in a tertiary alcohol without assuming that loading primarily broadens V2.

m17 at 2/1 and 50 ul fills a missing ordinary-regime point for trifluoroethyl acrylate. The predicted 7.00/8.87 mL interval is compact, while 071fc2962498be2a0922 provides the measured 5/1 low-loading reference. This helps calibrate onset-versus-finish movement within acrylates alongside the selected long-chain m18 control.

m166 at 2/1 and 100 ul establishes the lower-ratio member of a matched beta-diketone pair. Its predicted 4.70/13.00 mL interval can be compared with the measured m167 2/1 reference ea6260d7052cabfca181. The comparison tests the effect of the fused aromatic environment while retaining the fluorinated diketone motif.

m166 at 5/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 4.60/22.25 mL, preserving onset while finish grows relative to the selected 2/1 point. The measured weaker-eluent references 20acd2ae49790ab82053 and 80de1b57c56257d2ecae also retain early onset. This directly teaches an endpoint-specific response distinct from delayed-onset esters.

m182 at 1/1 and 100 ul anchors a fused ketone with an early onset and broad finish. Measured references 13aa7f454204d054a196 and d7603686249e1fb69a60 show this pattern at neighboring solvent conditions. The new point tests the predicted finish contraction to 16.65 mL and helps keep finish behavior separate from onset prediction.

m123 at 10/1 and 100 ul supplies an ordinary middle anchor between measured 5/1 and 20/1 points 89d7d7adb1fc72276b1c and 84d88494c6db5c1688d3. Its predicted onset is slightly earlier than the measured 5/1 onset. This point constrains the local curve before the selected 50/1 extrapolation.

m123 at 50/1 and 100 ul tests a predicted increase to 24.26/43.58 mL. Related dimethoxy aryl compounds differ substantially in the measured weak-eluent records f38088920e6edd19a62f and 199cdd47b9f05e12aaa1. Its label can teach substitution-sensitive ether response rather than relying on oxygen count alone.

m110 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 27.02/42.91 mL, with nearly the same finish as selected dimethoxybenzene m123 despite an extra methoxy group. The measured 10/1 reference 815afa4c05f8c4e7ef9c remains much earlier. This comparison tests transfer of weak-eluent response across closely related ether environments.

m35 at 20/1 and 100 ul tests the predicted 14.53/34.88 mL upturn for para-iodoacetophenone. The measured 5/1 reference 8200df9dd2dce17ed7d1 and recent 1/1 reference e9950c0bf61094f632c2 are ordinary. This extends a correctly identified carbonyl scaffold into weaker eluent and helps calibrate transfer among halogenated acetophenones.

hypotheses.content: As EA fraction decreases, onset and finish responses remain strongly scaffold-specific. Some compounds develop delayed onset, others retain early onset with a later finish, and some remain in the ordinary regime.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: QGeoGNN needs separate structure-condition relationships for onset and finish. A global correction toward late retention would damage ordinary rows and early-onset broad intervals.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the matched m98, m166, m199, and aryl-ether contrasts reveal delayed onset, finish-dominated growth, or an ordinary response under weaker eluent?

hypotheses.content: The previous hypothesis that increasing loading generally broadens V2 more than it changes V1, within a fixed scaffold and mobile phase, is too strong and requires further testing.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many current candidate predictions barely respond to loading, but measured loading-associated differences are irregular and can involve onset as well as finish. New controlled labels should teach conditional sensitivity without encoding a universal broadening rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m185 5/1, does tripling loading change onset, finish, both, or neither? Do the m45 and m51 loading extensions follow their existing local trends?

hypotheses.content: Ordinary-regime V2 calibration remains an acquisition target: recent early rows include substantial finish overprediction, while other ordinary rows are already accurate. Error direction should therefore remain local to scaffold and condition.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Improving overall Row accuracy requires supervision of common early intervals as well as rare late labels. Compact predictions can also expose useful finish-compression failures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected m18 and m71 common-condition points confirm their unusually compressed predicted finishes, and does m17 provide a transferable ordinary acrylate response?

hypotheses.content: Some nonmonotonic ester condition responses may be reproducible local relationships. A reversal is recorded for m75 at matched loading; the predicted turnovers selected for other ester scaffolds remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Chemical solvent-strength priors should guide interpretation without forcing monotonic labels where the supplied distribution contains reversals, plateaus, or unexplained variation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched-loading contrasts for m75 at 10/1 versus 20/1, m85 at 5/1 versus 10/1, m87 at 2/1 versus 5/1, and m92 at 5/1 versus 20/1 confirm the predicted endpoint turnovers?

hypotheses.content: The anomalous pure-EA m73 observation may be a local label inconsistency rather than a reusable cinnamate retention regime; its reversed endpoint ordering prevents a confident mechanistic interpretation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A severe historical error associated with an inconsistent label should not propagate an unsupported retention correction across unsaturated esters.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched 50-ul loading, do pure EA and 1/1 reproduce the predicted response reversal, or does the pure-EA point return to an ordinary interval?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes favor local endpoint calibration over a global late-retention correction. Several ordinary rows still overpredicted V2 by roughly 3-4 mL, including 1dfd819f5ad387a25ee7, 9138d3d29ef0d7169d74, and 4c15c048e4f33116df8d, whereas 5dfa7a7352e7a66c29e6 and b3e21424d2010c374094 were accurate. The matched m91 labels 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28 and a2ecf2b2f28094d70368 show modest increases in both endpoints from 2/1 to 5/1, rather than a newly demonstrated finish-only threshold. The large m87 overprediction in eed75e5b0d9c27fa754c motivates intermediate-condition measurements. The severe m73 error in 2732471e4009311396ed includes V1 greater than V2, so I treat it as an unresolved endpoint inconsistency and select neighboring conditions. Reviewing the full trajectory also weakens the previous monotonic loading-broadening claim: m177 at 50/1 has a late finish at 50 ul, an ordinary finish at 100 ul, and a late finish at 150 ul. These records establish irregular variation, not a causal loading threshold. I also correct earlier interpretation errors: higher PE/EA is weaker eluent, and 0/1 is pure EA. SMILES identify m87 as ethyl 4-methoxybenzoate, m35 as para-iodoacetophenone, m184 as nonfused 2,6-dibromobenzaldehyde, and m213 as dibenzyl ether. Loading solvents are taken from the condition arrays; for example, 58394a71418a9623e18a uses DCM.
batch_rationale: The batch emphasizes missing relationships within the supplied Row distribution, where eligible molecules are already represented in the observations. Matched solvent pairs test specific response shapes across cinnamate, fused ester, fluorinated aldehyde, sulfoxide, alpha-ketoester, malonate, substituted benzoate, fluorinated diketone, and aryl-ether environments. The m185 loading pair isolates one recorded variable, while m45 and m51 extend existing loading series. Ordinary m18, m71, and m17 points address finish calibration and compressed predicted intervals. The m97/m101 comparison tests closely related ester connectivity at similar sample amounts, and the m110/m123 comparison tests transfer across methoxy substitution patterns. These contrasts may improve generalization by teaching when onset and finish move together, when finish changes independently, and when a predicted turnover needs correction. Candidate aliases with identical tuples are avoided. Quantile ranges are treated cautiously: V2 q10 is zero throughout the supplied candidates and some V1 quantiles cross, so their widths are not used as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Historical acquisition errors motivate the scientific questions but are not treated as current-model residuals. No unrecorded concentration, flow, pH, or other conditions are assumed.
